Generalizes an existing convention rather than adding one, and matches what 2 of 3 runs already chose. Golden [intrans-stative]. M1 v6 unanimous.

Agent omitted it rather than force ConditionalProperty (which is only demonstrated for stative conditions, not action timing).

sentence: She sold it the following year.

sentence: Only the night shift reported the smell.
gap: group-only vs per-member rule for a bare uncounted collective-noun subject with an ordinary (non-collective) verb; the closest worked precedent ('the committee approved the plan') stays group-only, but the general distribution machinery could argue for adding a per-member rule
note: COST MEASURED 2026-08-03 (Tier A normalize arm): seedA-008 'A crew repairs a cracked feed pipe' — the ACTIVE was parsed as a per-member distribution Implication over crew members, the PASSIVE as a plain event, so the voice alternation failed to collapse. No longer a costless gap.
resolution: prompt: a SINGULAR collective noun is not a plural and does NOT distribute — one participant, plain event, no rule; reaching the members needs explicit wording ('every member of the crew', 'the crew members'). The trigger is GRAMMATICAL NUMBER, not whether the referent happens to be a group. Evidence: of 114 parsed records with a collective subject, 104 already did this and only 3 (the crew family) distributed — the convention existed, the prompt never stated it. Goldens [dist-collnoun-singular] + [dist-collnoun-members]; 2 e2e guards.

sentence: The registrar suspected the tally had been padded.

Same sealing mechanism, opposite conventions for in-seal referents.

sentence: The consignment might clear customs before Thursday.
gap: does an epistemic modal ALSO carry a tense/status atom? One run emitted (Might e) alone, another (Might e) + (Future e). Uncovered.
resolution: prompt: a bare epistemic modal is the event's ONLY status atom — no tense beside it (English present-tense modals are tense-neutral: 'she might be home now'). Tense only when the clause marks it independently.

sentence: The pump did not restart after the outage.
gap: does a NOMINAL event referent ('the outage') get its own tense atom? One run emitted (Past sk_outage_1), another did not. Uncovered.
resolution: prompt: an event-noun that is only a TEMPORAL ANCHOR in an adjunct gets its class atom + ordering relation and nothing else — no tense/status, since the clause predicates nothing of it. 'Before the inspection' shows why: (Past ...) would assert an inspection that may never happen.

sentence: The culvert flooded because the grate had clogged.
gap: OVER-GENERATION: one run emitted (PartOf sk_grate_1 sk_culvert_1), a part-whole relation the text never states. Should world knowledge licence unstated relational atoms? Current doctrine implies no.
resolution: prompt: new Core-patterns doctrine 'Assert only what the text states' (6th pattern) — world knowledge picks the READING, never adds content; culvert/grate given as the negative example; licensed exceptions enumerated (typing, compound genus, clause roles, TODAY calendar atoms, indefinite witnesses); test = 'point at the words that put the atom there'. Blind 10/10 (2 agents): target emitted no PartOf, and all 4 over-correction controls held.

sentence: Renata handed the surveyor a clipboard.
gap: SCOPE of the agent-nominalization rule is unstated. It says to expose the capability (Inheritance <nom> (can <verb>)) unconditionally, but both worked examples have the nominalization as the PREDICATE ('Penguins are swimmers'). Here 'surveyor' is an incidental referent; run7 emitted (Inheritance surveyor (can survey)), runs 8-9 did not. Same shape as gap-0002: a rule whose scope is unstated behaves like an optional one.
note: closed 2026-07-29; was the sole M1 v3 instability
resolution: prompt: agent-nominalization decomposition SCOPED to two triggers — (a) the symbol was fused from the surface (egg_layer, dam_builder), same licence as the compound genus since nothing else reaches a minted symbol, or (b) the nominalization is the COPULAR PREDICATE. A merely referring use (subject/object/appositive) is typed and left alone; surveyor~survey on a bare mention is deferred downstream like go_out~fail. Also added the missing trigger test (suffix must strip to a standalone verb AND 'an X is one who/that Vs' definitionally true — engineer/hydrologist/tenant/student fail). Checked first: the broad 'emit everywhere' rule would have forced adjudicating rooster/reactor/drawer/scooter/plumber/vendor and touched ~15 goldens. Every existing golden already conformed to the narrow rule — the convention existed, the prompt just never stated it. 2 goldens + 2 e2e guards. M1 v6: event-ditrans 0.333 -> 1.000, unanimous.

sentence: Only the night shift reported the smell.
gap: The modifier-exposure list enumerated purpose/association/role but not TEMPORAL noun modifiers, so 'night' fell outside every stated category: run10 emitted the genus only, run11 emitted NO decomposition at all, run12 emitted genus + (Inheritance night_shift night). Three different answers to one compound.
resolution: prompt: the modifier line is now PART OF SPEECH, not meaning — a noun modifier is never exposed whatever it names (purpose, association, role, time), an adjectival one always is; steel_beam vs wooden_bridge given as the contrast pair, and the genus itself stated as always emitted. Golden [decomp-kind-noun-mod].
note: the total-omission half was caused by a hedge I had just added to a Core pattern — see gap-0026

sentence: The culvert flooded because the grate had clogged. / The registrar suspected the tally had been padded.
gap: Past-perfect ordering was scoped BY EXAMPLE ('had V-ed when / by the time ...'), so a causal clause and an attitude complement were both undetermined. Third instance this session of the same defect: a rule whose scope is shown rather than stated behaves exactly like an optional atom.
resolution: prompt: scope replaced by a TEST — emit (Before ...) whenever the sentence contains another ASSERTED event to precede, whatever connective links them (temporal, causal, relative). Two carve-outs: nothing to order against -> no atom; inside a SEAL -> no atom, since ordering atoms never cross a seal boundary in either direction (follows from existing sealing doctrine). Both match the majority runs. Goldens [time-pastperf-causal] + [time-pastperf-sealed]. M1 v6: both items unanimous.
note: the last two disagreements at v5 0.933 were this one rule hit twice

sentence: The east wing was repainted last spring. / Only the night shift reported the smell.
gap: SELF-INFLICTED. My gap-0023 edit added 'each fires only where Compound decomposition says it does' to the 'Assert only what the text states' Core pattern. Inside a bullet whose whole thrust is do-not-over-emit, a qualifier reads as a caution — and two compound genus atoms went missing across runs.
resolution: prompt: reverted to a plain affirmative — the genus and capability atoms of a decomposed compound are 'always emitted, exactly as Compound decomposition specifies'. LESSON: in a Core pattern a qualifier reads as a caution, so hedging a mandatory rule there is functionally identical to marking the atom optional.
note: caught only because the v4 re-measure covered all 20 items, not just the one being fixed

sentence: Seven minus four make three. / Six times three is eighteen.
gap: An ARITHMETIC statement has no representation. The prompt uses `Compute` only inside QUERY patterns ((Compute > ($n 2) -> true)); asserting a mathematical fact is unspecified, so the parser improvised `(Compute * (6 3) -> 18)` — which puts a NUMERAL in head position, violating the head conventions (C4/C5 both fire).
note: 2 of 100 Tier B records. Needs a decision: assert arithmetic via Compute, or treat 'six times three' as a quantity term in a copular statement. Deferred — does not block mining.

sentence: A recipe requires two eggs. / Two eggs are required by a recipe.
gap: The BY-PHRASE role in the passive of a STATIVE transitive is undetermined. The active gives (Agent e recipe); the passive gave (Holder e recipe) — but the prompt reserves `Holder` for possession only, and states that a transitive subject is `Agent` even when inanimate. The two voices therefore produce different graphs for the same proposition.
note: found by the normalize arm, which is self-checking: base and its voice alternation must canonicalize identically
resolution: prompt: a passive carries exactly the roles its active would — a by-phrase takes the role the ACTIVE subject would have had, Agent even for a stative/inanimate causer, NEVER Holder (possession-only); an agentless passive just omits the atom. Stated as a checkable invariant: a voice alternation must produce the same atoms. Golden [role-passive-by].

sentence: An airline cancels the evening flight. / The evening flight is canceled by an airline.
gap: `cancel` is not in the #23 Theme-vs-Patient worked lists and the change-of-state test is unclear for it (a cancelled flight does not physically change, but it ceases to be scheduled). Active chose `Theme`, passive chose `Patient` — the exact same-verb-different-role failure the prompt warns about, since a statement and its question must pick the same role or QA misses.
note: same class as gap-0010 ('expire'): an unlisted verb where the change-of-state test does not decide
resolution: prompt: a state change need NOT be physical — when the object is itself an event or scheduled occurrence and the verb changes whether/when it happens (cancel, call off, postpone, delay, reschedule), the occurrence is altered -> Patient; verbs that merely evaluate or record (grade, inspect) stay Theme. Golden [role-occurrence-patient].

sentence: The chef bought several crates of lemons.
gap: A NESTED CONTAINER PARTITIVE — 'N containers of M' (several crates of lemons, a box of nails, two bags of cement) — has no stated representation, and the two parses disagree. run1 gave (GroupOf x crate-of-lemons)+(Member x crate), which makes ONE symbol both a group of lemons and a member of crate; run2 gave the coherent (GroupOf x0 crate)+(GroupOf x1 lemon)+(PartOf x1 x0). The measure reading ('a cup of water') and the partitive reading ('three of the presses') are both specified, but a COUNTED CONTAINER holding a substance/plural is neither.
note: Surfaced by the run1-vs-run2 re-parse diff, NOT by the fixes it was testing — 7 of the first 38 re-parsed records changed, all this one seed. run2 looks right; the rule just needs stating. Also visible: the counted-plural 'several crates' correctly gained a distribution Implication in run2.

sentence: A recipe requires two eggs. / A permit requires a countersignature.
gap: RULE COLLISION I INTRODUCED. The subject role of a STATIVE TRANSITIVE (require, need, contain, hold, lack) is claimed by two rules at once: 'a transitive subject is Agent even when inanimate and non-volitional' vs the stative branch I added last batch ('a stative ... takes Experiencer'). The stative clause says *intransitive*, but the parser applies it to transitive subjects too — two sibling seeds with the SAME verb split: seedA-016 base -> (Agent e recipe), seedA-017 base -> (Experiencer e permit). It also defeats the gap-0028 fix: the by-phrase stopped using Holder as instructed but went to Experiencer rather than Agent, so seedA-016's voice pair still mismatches.
note: 6+ records in the first 100. Fix is small — say explicitly that the stative branch is intransitive-only and a transitive subject is Agent regardless of stativity — but it is a NEW edit, so parked for the user.
resolution: prompt: stativity does NOT demote a transitive subject — a stative transitive still takes `Agent`; ONLY possession (own/have/lack -> Holder) and psych/perception (fear/believe/see -> Experiencer) move it. The `Experiencer` branch is stated as **intransitive-only**: it never reaches a subject that has an object. This was a collision I introduced — the stative-Experiencer clause (previous batch) and the transitive-Agent rule both claimed stative transitives. Golden [role-stative-transitive].

sentence: A shoreline survey begins at dawn. / The apple harvest begins in September.
gap: The present-tense FUTURATE rule fires inconsistently: 'begins at dawn' GAINED (Future e) in run2 while 'begins in September' LOST it. 15 of the first 100 records differ by exactly this one atom — the largest single category of change, and unrelated to any fix in this batch. The rule does not say which present-tense scheduled events count as futurate.
note: classic optional-atom signature: one atom, present in some parses and absent in others
resolution: prompt: a present-tense futurate now requires POSITIVE EVIDENCE the event is ahead — either a calendar time placeable after a supplied TODAY, or a lexically future adjunct (tomorrow/next week). With neither ('the survey begins at dawn', no TODAY) emit NO tense atom and let the default stand. Root cause: the rule depended on a reference time the corpus items never supply, so it was unapplicable-but-attempted — 15 of the first 100 re-parsed records differed by exactly this one atom. Golden [time-no-futurate].

sentence: A lathe requires monthly servicing.
gap: A generic requirement flipped REPRESENTATION between parses: run1 reified an event ((Member e require)+(Holder e lathe)+(Theme e servicing)); run2 emitted an opaque kind-relation (Require lathe monthly_servicing). Both are licensed reading-wise — the striking/relational-generic rule vs ordinary verbal predication — and nothing says which wins for a generic stative transitive.
note: 3 records; the two forms are not comparable by any graph metric, so this is worse for mining than a role difference
resolution: prompt: the kind-relation form's TRIGGER is now stated — BOTH arguments must be bare kind-denoting NPs (bare plural or mass). An indefinite/definite singular is an ordinary verbal clause and reifies an event. Stated with the reason: the two forms are not comparable (event-with-roles vs opaque binary atom), so a clause drifting between them yields two records with nothing in common. Golden [gen-relational-singular].

sentence: A countersignature is required by a permit.
gap: An indefinite singular ('a permit') was read as a KIND in the passive and given a distribution Implication over permits, while the active read it as a witness. Whether 'a N' is generic or existential is undetermined for stative/modal predications.
fix: 2026-08-04: negation-denial scope rule. `### Negation (events)` gains 'negation does not re-decide the subject' (indefinite/definite singular = witness; generic denial needs a bare plural or explicit quantifier) + 'a negated plural/group keeps both emissions'. `## Existential` replaces 'judge from context' with the copular-vs-verbal test, carving out deontic/capability (keyed on the modal, not the determiner). M1 0.857 -> 0.931; 3 target + 3 OUT-OF-SAMPLE negation controls all unanimous.
